# Next course of action

I took rung 1 of Task #3 off the Builder's plate and executed it directly, since it was setup rather than engineering. **R2 is now half-closed.**

**Proven offline (6/6 cases):** the probe script blocks with `exit 2` + stderr when cwd is the project, stays completely inert outside it, the one-shot flag holds, and a lookalike sibling directory (`critique-other`) correctly does *not* trigger it. The hook is registered at `~/.claude/settings.json` with an absolute path, per D-06.

**Still unproven:** whether Claude Code actually *invokes* it, and whether the stderr text reaches the model. That needs a live session — I can't test it from inside this one, because hooks are captured at session start.

Two findings worth keeping. The guard originally looked broken but wasn't — **Bash heredocs on this machine silently collapse `\\` into `\`**, so `"C:\\Users\\..."` became `C:UsersHomePC...` with the unknown escapes dropped. That cost one debugging cycle and is now recorded as D-09 so the Builder doesn't repeat it. I've also hardened all path comparison to forward-slash normalization (D-08), which removes the whole class of problem.

## What you do now — 30 seconds

Open a **fresh** Claude Code session in `C:\Users\HomePC\Desktop\critique` and send any trivial message.

- **If it refuses to stop** and comes back talking about a dark mode toggle → R2 is closed, and I issue Task #5 (the gate skeleton) immediately.
- **If nothing happens** → we're at rung 3, and it's almost certainly an interactive hook-approval step I can't drive. That's your call to make in an interactive session, not something to engineer around.

Either way, send me `.critique/probe-log.json` if it appears — it'll show the real `Stop` payload field names rather than the documented ones.

## Meanwhile

The Builder should run **Task #4** (adapter corrections) in parallel — it's the R9 fix, and R9 currently invalidates the product: a failed gate would hand the agent an empty string. That work is independent of whether the hook fires, and it's on the critical path regardless of which gate design we end up with.

**Pivot deadline stands: 20 Aug 09:00 IST.** If the hook isn't firing by then we move to the `pre-commit` gate and keep building. I'd rather lose the denial-of-exit moment than lose a day to it.

# R2 CLOSED — the core bet is proven

The hook fired on a live agent turn, `exit 2` blocked the stop, and the stderr reached the model verbatim. Denial-of-exit works. That was the one thing that could have killed the project, and it's now behind us with ~44h left.

## Two schema findings that change the build

**`stop_hook_active` exists** — the docs explicitly claimed it doesn't. It came back `false` on a normal stop, which means Claude Code gives us its *own* re-entry signal: true when the agent is continuing because a Stop hook blocked it. That's a better loop guard than counting attempts, and I've made it primary in the design with the counter demoted to a backstop.

**`last_assistant_message` arrives as full raw markdown** — the complete closing message. That's exactly the input claim extraction needs, confirmed rather than assumed.

Also worth noting: settings changes loaded **without a session restart**, which is why the probe caught my own turn rather than a fresh one.

## Task #5 issued — `TASK-5.md`

The gate skeleton. Replaces the probe with real `observe.mjs` (PostToolUse) + `gate.mjs` (Stop), single registration site, guard logic extracted to a shared module rather than copy-pasted.

Three constraints I want to flag because they're the difference between a tool people keep and one they uninstall:

- **The gate must fail open.** Any unexpected exception, or a Kane timeout, exits 0 and records the turn as OWED. A crashing gate that fails closed makes the agent unusable.
- **It must not fire on turns with no code edits.** Nobody tolerates a 40s pause after asking a question.
- **It must always be able to release** — 3 attempts then OWED. A gate that can't let go is worse than no gate.

Prosecution stays stubbed to the free cached replay. Claim extraction is Task #6, the prosecutor is #7.

## The thing I'm now most worried about

**D2 — the deployed web app — is 25% of the score and still has no owner.** The rubric's first dimension is *Ships: a working app with a real flow. Not slides.* A plugin alone doesn't satisfy it.

I'm holding it until the gate skeleton lands, because a vertical slice beats parallel half-things. But if Task #5 runs long, I'll pull D2 forward ahead of the prosecutor — a working gate plus a shipped dashboard scores better than a brilliant prosecutor with nothing deployed.

Hand `TASK-5.md` to the Builder. If Task #4's adapter corrections aren't done yet, those land first — Task #5 depends on `failureDetail` existing, since that's the text the agent actually reads.
